item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01685","case1_error":"Omits the $20 flat fee from the total deposit.","case2_error":"Unnecessarily divides Billy's already calculated 80% tip contribution by two.","reason":"The first omits a required fixed charge; the second applies an unsupported additional split to the correct contribution.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01686","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of accounting for loss in the purchased rope.","case2_error":"Subtracts mint plants from the basil-only subtotal and omits the surviving parsley plant.","reason":"The first applies loss to the wrong side of the length requirement; the second treats a category subtotal as the complete inventory.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01687","case1_error":"Uses doubled two-week vegetable consumption as a weekly amount before adding weekly kale.","case2_error":"Replaces the exact fourth-hour multiplier of 4/3 with 1.33, producing a fractional guest and towel count.","reason":"The first mixes time periods; the second introduces an inaccurate approximation of an exact fraction.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01688","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final profit $88 after correctly writing (16 × $8) − $30, which yields $98.","case2_error":"Treats the $2 price for five juice cans as a per-can price.","reason":"The first supplies an incorrect final number after a correct formula; the second uses an erroneous unit-price relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01689","case1_error":"Leading answer marker says 15, but the derivation and concluding answer correctly give 21 pancakes.","case2_error":"Assigns the friend's 40% rental share to John instead of John's remaining 60%.","reason":"The first has only an answer-marker conflict, so a shared mathematical error mechanism cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
